Fitted MPCurve models

Source: R/MPCurver-package.R
mpcurve.Rd

An mpcurve object contains the sample positions, feature trajectories, uncertainty estimates, and convergence diagnostics returned by fit_mpcurve or do_mpcurve. Use summary.mpcurve for a numerical summary and plot.mpcurve to visualize trajectories and sample orderings.

Sample positions

For a single ordering, $locations$mean$pseudotime contains posterior-mean positions on \([0,1]\), and $locations$map$pseudotime contains positions at the most probable grid component. For multiple orderings, $locations is a named list with one such record per ordering. Pseudotime represents relative position along an inferred trajectory; its direction can be reversed.

Single-ordering objects

For intrinsic_dim = 1, $params$pi is a length-K position-prior vector, $params$mu is a d x K posterior-mean trajectory matrix, $params$sigma2 is a length-d estimated variance vector (or NULL when measurement standard deviations are supplied through S), and $gamma is the n x K responsibility matrix. The full Gaussian trajectory posterior is available from $fit$posterior. When S is supplied, $measurement_sd stores either its length-d feature-shared form or its n x d observation-level form.

Multiple orderings and feature assignments

For intrinsic_dim = M >= 2, the variational family is $$q(C)\prod_{j=1}^d q(Z_j)q(U_j\mid Z_j).$$ Here \(C\) represents sample positions, \(Z_j\) the ordering followed by feature \(j\), and \(U_j\) its trajectory. The object contains:

  • $params$pi: named list of M length-K position-prior vectors;

  • $params$mu: named list of M d x K conditional posterior-mean matrices;

  • $params$sigma2: one shared length-d estimated variance vector, or NULL for known measurement noise;

  • $gamma: named list of M n x K position-responsibility matrices;

  • $measurement_sd: NULL when noise is estimated, or the supplied length-d / n x d known-standard-deviation specification;

  • $conditional_posterior: conditional Gaussian distributions for \(q(U_j\mid Z_j=m)\). Each $mean[[m]] is d x K; each $cov[[m]][[j]] is K x K; and $var[[m]] (also available as $diag[[m]]) is d x K;

  • $lambda_mat: a d x M matrix of smoothness parameters;

  • $partition$pi_weights: a d x M matrix containing \(q(Z_j=m)\), with the hard display assignment in $partition$assign;

  • $objective_history and $temperature_history: the variational objective and its temperature schedule. Use the \(T=1\) segment to assess convergence after annealing.

Each row of $partition$pi_weights sums to one. Concentrated rows indicate strong support for an ordering; diffuse rows indicate uncertainty about the feature assignment. Conditional trajectory means describe the fitted shape under each possible assignment, so interpret them alongside these probabilities.

Additional fields

$fit stores the underlying variational fit. For partition models, $fits provides derived per-ordering views for inspection; continue the complete model with do_mpcurve(object). The dimension fields $intrinsic_dim, $active_intrinsic_dim, and $displayed_intrinsic_dim all equal the specified M for structural partition fits.
